# MacVoice: full reference (llms-full.txt)

Official URL: https://macvoice.akshatt.in
Maker: Akshat Thakur (https://akshatt.in)
Version: 0.1.2 (November 2026)

> MacVoice is a private voice typing (dictation) app for Mac. Press a global shortcut (default Control + Option + Space) in any app, speak, and MacVoice types clean, punctuated text at the cursor. Speech recognition runs on the Mac using Apple's on-device SpeechAnalyzer engine (macOS 26+). It is free, with no subscription and no account.

MacVoice is a native Swift menu bar app (under 1 MB) made by independent developer Akshat Thakur. It is for anyone who writes a lot on a Mac (people who live in Slack and email, writers, developers, founders) and wants fast dictation that keeps their voice private.

## What it does
- **Types into any app**: Slack, Mail, Notes, Word, Google Docs and Notion in a browser, VS Code, Terminal and more. Text goes wherever the cursor is.
- **Keyboard input, not the clipboard**: MacVoice sends text as keyboard events (CGEvent). It never reads or changes the clipboard, and it works in most fields that block paste. It deliberately refuses to type when macOS Secure Input (password fields) is active.
- **Two modes**: Polished (default) removes fillers ("um", "uh"), stutters ("the the"), fixes missing apostrophes ("dont" → "don't") and capitalization, follows voice commands, and types one sentence at a time. Verbatim types exactly what was recognized, word by word, while you speak.
- **Voice commands** (Polished, English): "new line", "new paragraph", "bullet point", "comma", "question mark", "exclamation mark", "full stop", "period" (at the end), "semicolon", "shift enter", and "scratch that" (deletes the last sentence). Commands are ignored when clearly part of a normal sentence ("the next line of code").
- **Custom words and replacements**: list names and jargon so Apple's recognizer prefers those spellings; define "what I say => what to type" shortcuts.
- **Chat-safe line breaks**: in Slack, WhatsApp, Teams, Discord, Telegram, Messages, Signal, Messenger (and Slack/WhatsApp on the web), "new line" sends Shift+Return so messages are not sent early.
- **Terminal-aware**: in Terminal, iTerm2, Warp, Ghostty, kitty, Alacritty, WezTerm and Hyper, only fillers/replacements are applied; no capitals, no trailing period, never presses Return.
- **Context-aware spacing and capitalization**: reads up to 3 characters before the cursor (not stored) to add a space when needed and avoid capitalizing mid-sentence.
- **Other**: customizable shortcut, launch at login, sound cues, light/dark appearance, compatibility option to type one character at a time.

## Privacy
- Audio stays in memory during dictation and is never saved or uploaded. No transcript history.
- No analytics, no telemetry, no account. The app makes no network requests itself; macOS may download Apple's speech model for the user's language once.
- Saved data: settings, custom words and replacements, in local macOS preferences.

## Pricing
- Free: every feature, no account, no trial, no subscription, on any number of Macs. Optional one-time contributions (from $3) fund development; contributions have a 14-day refund.

## Requirements
- macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later. Built for Apple Silicon Macs.
- Permissions: Microphone (to hear you) and Accessibility (to type into other apps).
- Languages: the Mac's system language if Apple's on-device engine supports it. Full cleanup and voice commands are English-only.

## How it compares (checked November 2026; see vendors for current details)
- **Apple Dictation**: free and built in; no filler removal, custom replacements, or chat-safe line breaks.
- **Wispr Flow**: cloud-based AI dictation; inserts by clipboard paste and then restores the clipboard; free up to 2,000 words/week, Pro about $144/year.
- **Superwhisper**: local or cloud AI models; pastes text after you finish; free tier, Pro about $85/year or $249.99 lifetime.
- **MacVoice**: on-device, types as you talk, never uses the clipboard, free; requires macOS 26+ and has no AI rewriting.

## How it works (technical)
- Audio: captured with AVAudioEngine into in-memory buffers; never written to disk.
- Recognition: Apple SpeechAnalyzer / SpeechTranscriber (Speech framework, macOS 26+), on-device. Custom words are passed to the recognizer as contextual strings (up to 100).
- Transcript handling: only confirmed (non-provisional) text is typed, so already-typed text is never rewritten.
- Cleanup (Polished mode): a deterministic, rule-based Swift polisher (no AI model, no network), well under 1 ms per phrase.
- Output: text is sent as keyboard events via CGEvent (Accessibility permission). The clipboard (NSPasteboard) is never used. Secure Input is respected.
- Footprint: native Swift, no Electron, no Python, no bundled model; app download under 1 MB.

## Install
1. Download MacVoice.dmg (free) from https://macvoice.akshatt.in/download and drag MacVoice to Applications.
2. If macOS blocks the first launch: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (or run `xattr -cr /Applications/MacVoice.app`).
3. Allow Microphone, then enable MacVoice under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
4. Click into any text field, press Control + Option + Space, speak; press again to stop.

## FAQ
### What does MacVoice actually do?
You click into any text box on your Mac, press Control + Option + Space, and talk. MacVoice turns your speech into text and types it right where your cursor is, in whatever app you're using: Slack, Mail, Notes, VS Code, Google Docs in Safari or Chrome, and so on. Press the shortcut again to stop.

### How is MacVoice different from Apple's built-in dictation?
MacVoice uses Apple's own on-device speech engine, so recognition quality is in the same family. The difference is what happens after: MacVoice removes 'um' and 'uh', fixes missing apostrophes ('dont' → 'don't'), follows spoken commands like 'new line', 'bullet point' and 'scratch that', lets you teach it your own words and shortcuts, sends a safe line break in chat apps instead of pressing Send, and keeps shell commands untouched in Terminal.

### Does MacVoice use copy-paste? Will it change my clipboard?
No. Many dictation apps put the text on your clipboard and press Cmd+V for you (some then restore your old clipboard afterwards). MacVoice never uses the clipboard at all. It sends the text as keyboard input, the same way a keyboard does, so whatever you copied stays exactly as it was.

### Does it work in fields where pasting is blocked?
Usually, yes. Because MacVoice types the text as keyboard input instead of pasting it, websites that block paste generally accept it. Password fields are the exception: when macOS Secure Input is on, MacVoice deliberately refuses to type.

### What can I say to format text?
In Polished mode (the default) you can say 'new line', 'new paragraph', 'bullet point', 'comma', 'question mark', 'exclamation mark', 'full stop', or end a sentence with 'period'. Say 'scratch that' to delete the last sentence MacVoice typed. MacVoice is careful with these words: 'the next line of code' or 'a long period' are typed normally.

### Can it learn names and technical words?
Yes. In Settings → Words you can list custom words (names, product terms, jargon like 'Kubernetes') and Apple's recognizer will prefer those spellings. You can also add replacements, written as 'what I say => what to type', for example 'my email => name@example.com'.

### Does MacVoice send my voice or text to a server?
No. Speech recognition runs on your Mac using Apple's on-device engine. MacVoice has no analytics, no account, and no history: audio lives only in memory while you dictate, and nothing you say is saved to disk. The one exception is the first run, when macOS itself may download Apple's speech model for your language.

### Does it work in Terminal?
Yes. MacVoice recognises Terminal, iTerm2, Warp, Ghostty, kitty, Alacritty, WezTerm and Hyper. In those apps it only removes fillers: it won't capitalise your command, add apostrophes, add a trailing period, or turn 'new line' into Enter, so commands stay runnable.

### Which Macs and macOS versions are supported?
MacVoice needs macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later, because it is built on Apple's new SpeechAnalyzer engine that first shipped in macOS 26. It is designed for and tested on Apple Silicon Macs (M1 and newer).

### Which languages does it support?
MacVoice uses your Mac's system language if Apple's on-device engine supports it. English gets the full cleanup (fillers, apostrophes, spoken punctuation, 'scratch that'). Other supported languages are transcribed and capitalised, without the English-only cleanup rules.

### Why is the download so small?
MacVoice is a native Swift app (under 1 MB) that uses the speech engine already built into macOS instead of bundling its own AI model. If your Mac has never used on-device speech for your language, macOS downloads Apple's model once on first use.

### Can I change the keyboard shortcut?
Yes. Open MacVoice Settings from the menu bar, go to the Shortcut tab, click the shortcut button and press any combination that includes Control, Option or Command. If another app already uses it, MacVoice keeps your previous shortcut.

### Is MacVoice really free?
Yes. Every feature is free to download and use, with no account, no trial and no time limit, on as many of your Macs as you like.

### Will it stay free?
Everything MacVoice does today stays free. If paid Pro features are ever added, they'll be new features, and early supporters get them free.

### What do supporters get?
Any future MacVoice Pro features free, early builds before public release, and a direct line to the developer. Contributions are one-time, from $3, paid through Polar.

### Can I get a refund on a contribution?
Yes, within 14 days, no questions asked. Email akshatthakur22@gmail.com with your receipt.
